FROM THE EXECUTION UP

What a trace actually contains

Every page so far reads the proof from the theorem downward. This one starts from a real run: the sanity-check programs in SanityChecks.lean executed in Lean, their traces exported entry by entry. For each entry you see what the attacker sees, what only the proof sees, the action that appended it with the triple it had to satisfy, and the invariant that is now true at that index. Reads and pure computations are shown between the entries so each step's whole do-block is visible.

message, on the wire random bytes protocol event stored state compromise ⟨n⟩ unary length prefix in a serialised message named chips open to their term; hover for the definition

Names used on this page

The trace contains terms, not names. These labels are assigned here by matching the exported term structure, so xSk always means the random value generated at index 4 and k always means the hash of the normalised DH term.

Traces produced by scripts/ExportTrace.lean from the DyLean snapshot in this site's export. The annotations are editorial and link to the declarations they paraphrase.
